invoicingPolicy.deposit: Invoice deposit immediately on order confirmation — same day
invoicingPolicy.balance: Invoice balance on day of delivery completion or installation sign-off
invoicingPolicy.paymentTerms: 14 days net on all balance invoices for managed projects
invoicingPolicy.neverDelay: Delayed invoicing is the single most common cause of cash flow problems in project businesses — invoice immediately

overdueProcedure.day1: Invoice sent on completion day — attach signed delivery/installation confirmation
overdueProcedure.day10: Courteous reminder email with invoice attached
overdueProcedure.day14: Phone call to accounts payable or office manager
overdueProcedure.day21: Formal overdue notice — reference payment terms and late fee clause
overdueProcedure.day30: Escalate to director/CEO contact. Consider pausing any new orders for this client.
overdueProcedure.day45plus: Legal letter of demand if unresponsive. Engage debt collection only after exhausting direct contact.

accountsReceivable.lateFeeClause: Include in all proposals and invoices: 'Invoices unpaid after 14 days attract a 1.5% per month late payment fee on the outstanding balance'
accountsReceivable.creditChecks: For projects above $80,000 with an unknown client, request a credit reference from their bank or use a commercial credit check service before order placement

supplierPaymentTerms.standard: 30% deposit on order placement, 70% against Bill of Lading (before release of goods)
supplierPaymentTerms.target: Negotiate Net 30 or Net 45 payment terms on balance with trusted suppliers
supplierPaymentTerms.neverPay: Never pay 100% upfront to a new supplier before goods are confirmed at port

accountsPayable.paymentSchedule: Process all supplier payments on Tuesdays — consistent schedule reduces administrative overhead and aids cashflow forecasting

supplierRelationships.earlyPaymentDiscount: Some suppliers offer 1–2% discount for payment within 7 days of BoL — take this offer if cashflow permits; it compounds significantly over annual volume
supplierRelationships.latePaymentImpact: Late payment to key suppliers risks production delays on next order — protect relationships by paying on time even when cash is tight

freightAndCustoms.customsBroker: Receive customs duty invoice within 3–5 days of goods arriving at port. Pay within 5 business days to avoid goods release delays.
freightAndCustoms.freightForwarder: Confirm payment terms at relationship establishment — many require prepayment or credit facility for first 3–6 months

bankReconciliation.frequency: Weekly minimum — daily during high-volume periods
bankReconciliation.purpose: Catch errors, confirm deposits received, confirm supplier payments cleared
bankReconciliation.tool: Xero, MYOB, or QuickBooks — all integrate with major Australian banks for automatic reconciliation
